title: vision->vision transfer: frozen DomainNet-32 SPM encoder -> Flowers-102 (bounded S1, five-shot)
question: Does the frozen DomainNet-32 SPM code construction (sealed M142 C2: 6x6 patches, ZCA whitener, 1923 atoms, 21-bin pyramid, width 40383) transfer to Oxford Flowers-102 under the same exact ridge read?

verdict.metric: test accuracy (306 rows) per penalty, best-penalty per arm
verdict.transfer_holds: SPM best-penalty test accuracy >= baseline best-penalty test accuracy
verdict.consequence_pass: transfer holds: the DomainNet SPM construction's codes read Flowers-102 at least as well as the cached backbone CLS features under the same ridge read
verdict.consequence_fail: scoped negative for THIS encoder: the SPM-1923 construction does not transfer to Flowers-102 five-shot; the deep-patch deployment arm (M176c-c1) is unaffected (registered)

disclosures: Not a matched-cost fight: baseline width 384 vs SPM width 40,383.
The baseline reads full-resolution images (cached ONNX DINOv2 CLS features); the SPM arm reads 32x32 images. Information mismatch in the baseline's favour, disclosed.
The SPM arm codes are the RAW C2 output (no power-normalisation; C4's transform was measured on DomainNet only).

corpus.provenance: verbatim copy of experiments/configs/v16/m142_c2.json corpus section (the encoder pin depends on this exact corpus)

sparse.provenance: verbatim copy of experiments/configs/v16/m142_c2.json sparse section (the encoder pin depends on these exact seeds)

encoder_pin.note: max-abs delta vs the sealed memmap must be EXACTLY 0.0 (bit-exact); any nonzero -> VOID

flowers.resize: PIL BILINEAR (the DomainNet parquet pipeline's own filter)
